desert_p22_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_001.text: The cargo of names arrived in a box smaller than the rumours had prepared town to expect. Han's receiving clerk had cleared a dry bench for the two returning carts, and the municipal records staff waited beside it with the conservator's handling space ready. Six adults and four mules came through the gate on the sixth travel day, tired, dusty and complete. Gao dismounted slowly, her replacement rod still in its padded slot. Du carried only the modern field folder. The secured old sheets rode in the strapped custody carrier where the actual support plan required them.

desert_p22_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_002.text: Yue counted faces before she looked at the box, then found herself smiling at its modest size. The return stock was three hundred and sixty-eight usable litres, one hundred and eighty-four in each tank, including the two protected hundreds still sealed. The daily actual draws had been one hundred and three, one hundred and five, one hundred and four, one hundred and eight, one hundred and five, and one hundred and seven: six hundred and thirty-two from the initial thousand. No well or channel water had been added.

desert_p22_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_003.text: The remaining fuel was ten kilograms from thirty purchased, twenty actually used for the six-day work and meals. Han checked the arithmetic with Gao and both drivers. The figures gave the visit a bounded journey rather than turn a successful paper arrival into proof that supplies never mattered. The six-day term had held its planned two working days between four travel days. The team used the current repaired cart approach under the responsible notice and rechecked it on arrival and departure. The low footbridge remained closed; no paper task needed anyone to cross it.

desert_p22_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_004.text: Tuo listened to the route account from the receiving bench and asked about one outer turning stone. Gao described its present condition. The guide had been right to remember it and right to ask again. Bao stayed out of the staff's custody handover, joining only when the travellers wanted their ordinary fatigue and minor abrasions reviewed. The old pages had arrived, but the people could still be the first practical concern.

desert_p22_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_005.text: The conservator transferred nine supported sheets and one small associated wrapper fragment under the district inventory. The original loose fragment from the first visit was already in municipal custody and listed separately, never counted again as a new recovery. Some sheets could be read fully after controlled handling; others retained gaps. The remaining materials stayed protected at the relay, with condition and location recorded for a later professionally scoped visit. She gave the receiving staff the transport environment and handling sequence, then watched the carrier open only in the prepared room. Du stood outside the marked space with empty hands.

desert_p22_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_006.text: The cargo had names in it, but no private map office had acquired the people those names once belonged to.

desert_p22_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_007.text: Gao had found the drainage grade sheet readable in place, though too fragile for immediate transport. Her copy preserved the visible reference terms and gaps, with measured site positions attached. The old bypass in the shallow wall plan matched a work description in that sheet. Its seasonal use had relieved the main throat under particular settings, not served as a limitless alternative channel. The present bypass was partly blocked and altered by later silt. Its restoration required current levels, structural assessment and responsible operating rules, not merely copying the old setting.

desert_p22_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_008.text: Gao's disappointment at that qualification lasted less than it would have a month earlier. She had a useful past and a present job for it.

desert_p22_009.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p22_009.text: The old sheet gives us a starting sequence and the places the workers meant to compare. It does not authorise me to put today's water through a buried run. I have copied the visible grades, marked the missing ones and tied the references to the current survey. The route authority can commission the full receiving assessment with the households represented. That is more work, not less. I am pleased anyway. We found why the bypass existed and why the modern map had lost it.

desert_p22_010.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p22_010.text: Now a person proposing to use it can be asked a better question than whether an old blue line looks convenient.

desert_p22_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_011.text: Du's missing household sequence occupied three of the nine supported sheets. They named fourteen historical household entries, while Onion Hollow now had eleven occupied compounds. The difference reflected a long period of departures, unions and changed identifiers, not three current families erased because a printer preferred a rounder map. The records staff would compare living claims with the old entries privately. Du could publish the historical count and source method without printing every family balance. The well keeper's sister appeared under the grandmother's contribution pattern in the transferred account, but the later settlement still needed the municipal register.

desert_p22_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_012.text: The field sheets strengthened a comparison already underway; they did not replace it with a dramatic verdict. One family name had lost its middle character to a tear. Du thought he remembered the full name from an old inventory. The apprentice, now helping the modern wrapper under paid time, asked where that inventory could be checked. He gave the reference. The missing character stayed a gap in the transcript until the separate source was examined. Yue watched the blank remain visible on the clean page.

desert_p22_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_013.text: It was the sort of space a storyteller could fill in a breath and an office might spend a week proving. The older patient's family wanted the truth of its own entry. They did not need Du to complete a neighbour's name because incomplete names made him uncomfortable.

desert_p22_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_014.text: The apprentice had prepared the corrected map's paid circulation account for his return. Du looked at its totals, source wrapper and current date policy, then asked whether she had encountered trouble. She said customers had wanted everything simpler and the printer had wanted everyone gone before sunset. Neither fact had destroyed the office. She had released the checked strips under his written authority and recorded the changes required by the actual well reopening. He read the last release entry and complimented her judgment before her handwriting. Her face changed so quickly that Yue nearly looked away.

desert_p22_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_015.text: Recognition was arriving at the task the apprentice had actually performed, where she had been waiting for it.

desert_p22_016.speaker: du_she
desert_p22_016.text: I was expecting to come home and rescue the office from decisions made in my absence. That is an ugly thing to admit after asking you to make them. The account shows the office did its work. I have brought new sources that will require another revision, and I would like you to lead the wrapper and reader order again under the agreed pay. Then tell me what you want next. I heard you talking about a room of your own before I left, and pretended you meant upstairs.

desert_p22_017.speaker: du_she
desert_p22_017.text: I have spent enough time lately discovering what happens when I choose the convenient meaning of somebody else's words.

desert_p22_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_018.text: The apprentice said she wanted to open a small independent practical press after the next term, beginning with household and local route sheets rather than an atlas. She would need savings, a modest equipment lease and permission to use only the material she actually owned or licensed. Du's office could commission work from her instead of retain her indefinitely as an apprentice. He listened, looking bereaved again, and then asked about her proposed room. It was above the stationer, with good light and a rent she had checked herself.

desert_p22_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_019.text: Yue recognised the tone in which a wish had become a room with a bill. Du did too. He asked for her written plan, this time to help rather than reinterpret it.

desert_p22_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_020.text: The rival publisher arrived with a request to see the new findings before the public release time. He had paid a contribution and hoped that meant an early private advantage. Gao showed the equal-release clause he had signed. The public findings would be available together after condition and transcription checks. He could inspect the modern current route account already released to everyone. He accepted the limit, then asked whether a second print run would now be needed. The apprentice said yes, but the date strips could carry current changes while the historical back awaited the checked sequence.

desert_p22_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_021.text: The practical manufacturing choice had saved a great deal of paper. The printer would be unbearable about being right.

desert_p22_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_022.text: At the courtyard, the older patient heard the returning team's count before any claim result. Six adults and four mules, all back. She nodded, perhaps remembering the first morning when her garden looked like work that could simply be finished. Du visited after rest with the modern extract and the conservator's public condition note. He did not bring original old paper to a bedside where soup and mirrors crowded the table. The patient followed the grandmother's entry with her finger, reading the full copied season where the receipt had only an abbreviation. Her daughter read beside her.

desert_p22_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_023.text: They asked the questions that belonged to the family, not the ones that would make a better printed discovery. The later settlement comparison showed a remainder recorded for the historic household, pending a receiving acknowledgement that had never been closed. That was enough to justify a present review under the district's rules, not enough to announce a cash award or current ownership of the well. The family representative submitted the extract, receipt and lineage account through the ordinary hearing process. The present community maintained collective source use under its existing arrangement. Du explained both matters separately.

desert_p22_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_024.text: The patient smiled at the grandmother's stubborn mark and said she would have liked the clerk who wrote pending. Pending was better than pretending the account had vanished. Then she asked for her tea before the word grew cold. The conservator visited the courtyard later without a box. She wanted to hear the sleeping-jars term from the older woman herself for the contextual note, with permission to quote it. The patient allowed the term and described the seasonal cleaning work. She did not permit the family balances in a public caption.

desert_p22_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_025.text: The conservator accepted the distinction and asked how the grandmother tied a cloth over a jar lid against dust. The niece fetched a modern scrap to demonstrate. Her shoulder tolerated the light gesture; no one recruited it for a larger task. Yue watched ordinary hands give the old sheet something the sheet could not preserve alone: the way a knot had been tightened at the court before a dry season. The conservator's condition report named what had been recovered, what remained unread, which surfaces required support and which site conditions needed continued care.

desert_p22_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_026.text: Du wanted one sentence saying the archive had been saved. She offered the actual nine-sheet transfer and protected remaining material instead. He accepted it after a visible little struggle. The patient, listening, said a well was kept in the same way: by describing the parts that worked and fixing the parts that did not, not claiming the whole thing forever. The conservator laughed and asked permission to use that line too. The woman said only if the mapmaker's embarrassing face was included, which proved impossible within the written report.

desert_p22_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_027.text: The young worker met the municipal driver at the receiving yard with the school date. The driver had returned in time for his brother's assessment appointment and was pleased enough to forget his tired boots. Both applicants had their own forms and household contributions; neither would borrow the other's grant application as if kinship were a stamp. They arranged to go to the counter together the next morning. Yue gave the young worker his modern course enquiry copy, returned from the travelling folder where it had been protected.

desert_p22_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_028.text: His finger dressing was now small, his permitted hand use growing under review. He flexed the hand gently, then kept the paper away from the dusty cart rail. Han closed the funded conservation visit's immediate wage account at the actual return. The six travelling adults were paid under their terms, including professional handling and condition work whether or not all the box could be read. The nine sheets and copied grades fulfilled part of the scope; the protected remainder belonged in future planning. The drivers' returned stock, hired supports and town service obligations were checked before their terms ended.

desert_p22_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_029.text: Du's contribution did not buy a private shelf for the originals. The rival's did not buy early release. Han explained the final charges in his plain brown coat, then put the household basil errand on top of the completed invoices and went home.

desert_p22_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_030.text: Gao asked Yue to read the current receiving summary as a person who had walked the first two journeys and remained in town during the third. The distinction mattered. Yue could verify the first field positions and rescue arrangements from her own experience; the conservation trip's actual observations belonged to its travelling witnesses. She marked where the summary had slipped into we for work she had not seen. Gao changed the pronoun and named the team. Yue felt oddly relieved.

desert_p22_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_031.text: She had been part of the novel without being secretly present in every chapter, and the report could allow that too. The completed summary sounded less grand and more like people actually moving through time. Tuo reviewed the new current route panel after her ordinary local hire, a short guide consultation on firm town ground cleared within her recovery limits. She earned a modest fee and came back with no renewed swelling or pain. Bao recorded the good response without declaring every rough carrying task assessed.

desert_p22_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_032.text: Tuo then sat at the map table and found the historical winter shelter still appropriately bare in the artist's view. She approved, looking almost annoyed not to have an obvious correction. Du offered her tea and ginger. She asked whether he had practised buying the right one while travelling. He said no, but the market had developed the ability to recognise his mistakes.

desert_p22_033.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p22_033.text: The valley will still be difficult next winter. A current map can help people ask the right keeper and avoid the wrong roof; it cannot promise a season in advance. Put the receiving references where a driver can find them, and retain the household names only where permission and present use allow. The old community count can stay historical. I am not going to stand at a crossing reciting fourteen families to somebody whose mule wants its supper.

desert_p22_034.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p22_034.text: I will be glad to say that the well has a keeper, the path has a current notice and the office now knows how to admit when those have changed.

desert_p22_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_035.text: Bao brought the pilot room's first review note to the same table. It had seen more ordinary work complaints on its posted days and referred one case through the functioning transfer route. Supplies were adequate for the limited schedule; a shelf arrangement needed improvement and the attendant needed another supervised intake session. The board approved continuation for the next stated interval, with the budget and staffing unchanged unless reviewed. Gao asked whether Bao was pleased. She said yes, then asked why pleased always made people expect a speech. Tuo handed her tea.

desert_p22_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_036.text: The room's professionals sat quietly for a minute, each holding a cup whose work was merely to be warm.

desert_p22_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_037.text: The public release of the conservation findings drew fewer treasure hunters than the first rumours had. Most visitors wanted the route panel, source status or family enquiry reference. The artist's measured room view attracted a boy who asked whether the light line moved. Gao explained the observed opening and time without turning it into a magic key. The boy went to the window and watched the afternoon sun cross the floor there. Yue thought this a better practical response than buying a palace story. The rival publisher sold several useful sheets and looked less disappointed than he had predicted.

desert_p22_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_038.text: Ordinary interest could be commercially adequate if somebody gave it an honest shape.

desert_p22_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_039.text: One carrier demanded the community well be marked public free water because the map now showed it clearly. The apprentice directed him to the current local service and keeper's terms. A visible source did not become an unlimited travelling sale. The carrier grumbled, then asked where he could obtain a confirmed fill on his planned route. Han's clerk gave him the municipal yard's actual reservation process and the current receiving contacts beyond. The man left with a workable plan instead of a flattering assumption. Yue watched him fold the sheet.

desert_p22_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_040.text: It had cost him more thought than a bright blue dot, and might cost his animals much less trouble.

desert_p22_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_041.text: The older patient sent a short note to the well keeper through the confirmed carrier. It gave the family hearing date, the modern extract's existence and her continued care, then asked whether the new rope had become everyone's excuse to draw too much at once. The keeper's reply would take its own journey. Her daughter read the note back before sealing it, smiling at the familiar scold. Yue took the wrapper to the dispatch table under its ordinary fee. The patient had not become only a person receiving information from offices.

desert_p22_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_042.text: She still had a voice travelling outward, toward a community where her bed was absent and her work remained part of the court.

desert_p22_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_043.text: The records clerk prepared the hearing packet from supported modern extracts, source references, the family receipt copy and district rules. The originals remained in controlled custody, accessible through the responsible staff rather than passed around a crowded meeting. Du's apprentice checked the wrapper order; Gao checked the current observations she owned; Bao kept clinical records apart from public testimony. Yue was invited to attend as a witness to the first two field journeys if she wished, with paid travel and time provided under the hearing rules. She accepted the narrow witness role.

desert_p22_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_044.text: It would ask her what she had seen, not what she could imagine from the cargo that had arrived without her. Han's daughter asked whether a hearing was like a classroom in which everybody believed they were the teacher. Han said sometimes, and it would help if somebody kept the questions on the board. She offered to copy the public sequence large enough for the back bench, on a paid bounded preparation task. The chair agreed through the receiving clerk. Yue saw the daughter plan the headings from the actual source list, leaving private balances for the family room.

desert_p22_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_045.text: The wheel-and-flower signboard stayed at home. In the hearing's plain large letters, her own work would be visible without borrowing her father's expedition or somebody else's injury for importance. Late light touched the old box's receiving shelf while the municipal staff closed the handling room. The nine sheets lay supported under their covers, the first fragment listed separately, the unresolved lines still unresolved. Outside, town carts crossed the same paving they had crossed before anyone knew Onion Hollow's name. Yue walked with Du as far as the corner.

desert_p22_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_046.text: He said the cargo had been smaller than he expected and heavier after reading. She asked whether he meant the paper. He shook his head, then laughed at himself before the metaphor grew tiresome. The apprentice was waiting for his written reply about her independent room. That, too, was a name he needed to let take its own place.

desert_p22_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_047.text: The older woman asked Yue to stop calling her the patient when the clinician was not asking a clinical question. In the court, she said, Aunt Su would do. The hearing clerk could receive her full private name through the proper family form. Yue repeated the chosen address, and the woman smiled with a pleasure so immediate that it made the earlier role labels feel heavy. The niece rolled her eyes and said her aunt had always considered names a useful tool for controlling a room.

desert_p22_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_048.text: Aunt Su replied that the niece should learn to use her own before the latch workshop assigned her a permanent tray number. The mirror caught both their smiles. Aunt Su wanted the hearing arranged so she could speak without standing on the supported leg. The chair offered a seated place, a shorter attendance interval and a pause for care if required. Her daughter would accompany her, with the qualified short transfer booked through the clinic's existing service. The family balance discussion belonged in a smaller session, separate from the public route account.

desert_p22_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_049.text: Aunt Su accepted that arrangement and rehearsed the first sentence she wanted to say. It named the grandmother's actual contribution and asked for the unclosed account reviewed. She practised no accusation beyond what the extracts supported. Then she asked whether she could bring a plum preserve spoon to bribe the chair. The daughter said no. The niece wrote her own preferred address on the local work ledger after the latch maker asked. He had been calling her garden girl, kindly enough and inaccurately enough to irritate her.

desert_p22_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_050.text: She told him she could still work in a garden and wanted her name on the wages. He corrected the entry. At the court she showed Aunt Su the new line without making a grand claim about apprenticeship. Her short sorting term continued within the shoulder plan; a later task review would decide what she could learn next. The black thumbprint beside the wage receipt made her aunt laugh. Somebody had finally paid for the habit of finding small mistakes.

desert_p22_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_051.text: The young worker returned from the school's remaining entry assessment with the municipal driver's brother. Both had been assessed on their own eligible tasks, with current hand limits respected. The worker's ordinary training grant was approved for a stated part of the first term; his household contribution covered the rest, paid through the school's account. The term would begin next month after the scheduled medical clearance and preparation. He had a place, conditional on the ordinary enrolment requirements, rather than a lifetime trade granted by one rescue. He told Aunt Su at the courtyard and finally allowed himself to grin.

desert_p22_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_052.text: She demanded the exact starting day so she could complain in advance about him being late.

desert_p22_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_053.text: The municipal driver listened to the two students plan their first week and looked at his own road dust with satisfaction. His larger field fee had helped his brother's contribution arrive on time. It had not made the school require less work. He thanked Gao for the bounded hire and requested no immediate new trip. His next days belonged to the municipal employer and the family arrangements already waiting. Gao accepted that. The other driver likewise went home with the agreed payment and actual arrival note.

desert_p22_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_054.text: Han's yard grew quiet as the animals entered ordinary care and the carts lost their travelling covers. People had returned to lives the expedition had never owned.

desert_p22_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_055.text: The rival publisher's first compensation meeting was less cheerful than the map release. The younger guide from the original rescue had submitted her account of following the shortened card, the handcart damage and lost work. The correspondent's actual letter had described empty handcarts in dry conditions; the printed instruction overstated that observation. The ground had also changed after fresh drainage, which the earlier letter could not have witnessed. The district mediator proposed a review of the causal record and the repair costs, including the guides' own decisions and current recovery. The rival representative wanted a quick release form instead.

desert_p22_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_056.text: The guide read it and declined to settle what she did not yet understand. Her mother had brought the blue shawl again, folded neatly beneath the seated place. The guide asked the mediator to explain the release in plain terms. It would close later claims about the same incident in exchange for the offered amount. The repair estimate covered the cart's wheel and axle, while the offered sum did not fully cover even that known cost. She asked for the proposal in writing and a separate appointment to review it.

desert_p22_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_057.text: Du sat nearby as a source witness and did not advise her to take gratitude for money. Gao supplied the dated current observations. Yue watched the woman own a decision that belonged to her recovery as much as the support on her leg. The rival representative objected that correcting his card had already cost him enough. The mediator said correction and compensation answered different questions. He could dispute the causal share through the evidence review; he could not make a paid warning strip serve as an injured customer's agreement. The man looked angry, then tired.

desert_p22_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_058.text: His office was small too, its paper bills real, its error larger than it had expected. The guide said she did not want the office destroyed. She wanted a repair and lost-work proposal that admitted the actual instruction mattered. The mediator wrote that aim down and scheduled the next discussion with the real estimates attached. Afterwards the guide told Yue she was afraid of becoming difficult to hire. A map office could call a complaining guide careless and make clients believe it.

desert_p22_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_059.text: Yue said the office could say many things; the record would contain the actual letter, printed card, source limits and changed ground. The guide nodded, still afraid but less alone. She had a paid home task and a cart maker's plan, both waiting on recovery rather than publicity. She asked Yue to carry one copy to her partner, who was at the ordinary receiving yard. Yue agreed to that exact errand and left the larger legal advice with the mediator qualified to give it.

desert_p22_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_060.text: Han's overdue grain payment finally arrived as a partial settlement with a dated plan for the remainder. The amount matched the client's resale account, not Han's earlier wishful reading. He entered the money as received and left the rest outstanding. His mother watched him resist calling the whole bill settled. The daughter counted the actual coins against the firm reserve while he prepared the receipt. A few safer service inspections could now proceed without squeezing the next hire. He looked relieved, then admitted relief was not the same as having no risk. The household basil had survived both plantings.

desert_p22_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_061.text: For tonight they chose to discuss that more manageable victory.

desert_p22_062.speaker: han_xun
desert_p22_062.text: I had begun to hate that client's envelope before I knew what it contained. Today it contained real money and a real date. I will still check the next date when it comes, instead of turn this partial payment into a private prophecy. The firm can meet its present commitments. My mother says that sounds like a man asking to be applauded for paying bills. She is right. We will celebrate with supper because supper was going to happen anyway, and I will leave the reserve page open until my daughter has checked it.

desert_p22_063.speaker: han_xun
desert_p22_063.text: The flower signboard can wait until tomorrow. The basil cannot; somebody remind me before I pretend you already have.

desert_p22_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_064.text: Du reviewed the apprentice's independent-room plan after the returning cargo accounts closed. Her savings could cover the deposit; a modest equipment lease would cover a small press rather than the entire machinery she admired. She requested permission to use specified modern source wrappers she had prepared, with credit and licence terms, while old originals remained under public custody. Du agreed to commission two bounded jobs from the future room and put the rates in writing. He did not make the agreement conditional on her staying his apprentice forever.

desert_p22_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_065.text: She thanked him, then asked for a reference that described her judgment as well as her penmanship. He wrote it slowly, crossing out an unnecessary possessive before her name.

desert_p22_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_066.text: The conservator came for the receipt counterpart confirming her settled field and handling fee. Du offered an extra gratitude amount; she declined it and asked him to put the contribution toward responsible care of the remaining relay material. He did, through the district's actual conservation provision. The onion-skin flower remained on her umbrella handle, brittle now but still intact beneath a small protective wrap. Yue asked whether she would replace it. The woman said perhaps when it broke, and she preferred to know which part had actually broken first.

desert_p22_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_067.text: Du laughed, then watched her leave with the umbrella and his ledger balanced to a future task rather than a compliment.

desert_p22_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_068.text: Gao's new route assessment proposal was accepted for a later seasonal window, with the current channel grades, old bypass references and household concerns all in its scope. She would not lead it alone; the responsible water and structural staff would carry their own decisions. The fee and term were clear enough that she could budget ordinary life between jobs. She bought the finer instrument coupling she had admired earlier only after checking the new income was committed and the household bills paid. Yue teased her about finally owning the attractive metal. Gao said beautiful metal deserved no immunity from calibration.

desert_p22_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_069.text: She took it to the maker's reference bench before showing it to anybody else. At the instrument shop, the coupling passed its specified checks, and Gao marked the record with visible delight. She kept the plain working rod too, useful and already known. Du asked whether the new part would make her next survey perfect. She told him to stand still long enough for her to measure the size of that foolish question. The maker laughed and placed both rods in their proper carriers. Yue touched neither without permission, but admired the clean thread and small seat.

desert_p22_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_070.text: There were ambitions in this town that did not require a ruin or a rank. One could be a surveyor wanting an excellent tool and enough work to keep using it honestly.

desert_p22_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_071.text: Bao's pilot room needed a restocking visit before its next staffed afternoon. The attendant prepared the ordinary inventory correctly, then caught a counting error in dressings and called Bao before ordering. The clinic supplier corrected the invoice and improved the joke about the desert drying everything. This time he said dry paper still cost money. Bao said at least the joke had an invoice attached. Yue carried a light sealed parcel under a paid errand term and returned its receipt to the attendant. The room's budget remained finite, its care no less useful for that.

desert_p22_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_072.text: On the next open day, people would find the stated service rather than a vague promise growing somewhere behind a clean sign. Auntie Reed's hearing attendance was confirmed through the collective's actual notice. She would travel on the next market wagon, with paid witness time and ordinary return provision. Her grandson would stay home with family during the hearing rather than be dragged through a whole day of adults arguing about water. The grandmother's reply included a small dry reed tied into the wrapper, the kind used to show the crop's pith on the first journey.

desert_p22_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_073.text: Gao asked whether it should be preserved as a specimen. The claimant said it was only a reminder and would bring a fresh local sample if the officer required one. They left the reed on the table, where it cast a very thin shadow across the receiving date. The hearing chair received public questions before the formal session. One accused the caravan of withholding all its protected water from a community in trouble. Gao prepared the prospective stock calculation rather than answer from the comfort of knowing the actual return quantity.

desert_p22_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_074.text: Three hundred transferred left five hundred and ten for twelve adults, four mules, two travel days, medical variation and protected contingency. The community's actual clean capacity and separate household stores were also in the record, along with the urgent supply requests. Whether the choice had been reasonable would be discussed from what people knew then. The neat final two hundred and thirty-four could not travel backward and tell the morning's decision how much heat to expect.

desert_p22_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_075.text: Yue read that question and felt anger before she felt confidence. She had stood beside the vessels while water moved from a travelling tank into the household cisterns; now a stranger made the same scene sound like a refusal. Han asked whether she wanted him to answer first. She said no, she wanted the actual question separated from its accusation. Gao could explain the calculation. The keeper could explain community storage and receiving need. Yue could explain what was transferred and what she saw. She did not have to defend every person by becoming everybody's witness.

desert_p22_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_076.text: Han gave her a clean modern sheet, and she wrote those three tasks down.

desert_p22_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_077.text: The younger guide asked for the printed-card dispute kept distinct from Aunt Su's historic household account. The chair agreed. Both arose from the broader route enquiry, but one involved a recent instruction and injury, the other a transferred contribution with living review rights. The grass crop claim had its own measured junction and damage questions. The session would share the source chronology where relevant and use separate decisions. Yue checked the order on the public board. For once the town's three stories would meet a room prepared to keep them three long enough to understand how they connected.

desert_p22_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_078.text: The board's large letters could be read from the back bench.

desert_p22_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_079.text: On the evening before the hearing, Aunt Su sat with her full private name form in the small bowl beside the bed. The public room would hear the chosen address she permitted and the facts she wished to give. The family session would receive the lineage papers. Her daughter checked the qualified transfer time; the niece checked the support and ordinary meal plan. Yue brought the household letter carrier's actual receipt. Aunt Su asked whether the well keeper had replied. Not yet. She accepted that and put the receipt with the bowl.

desert_p22_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_080.text: Messages still needed roads, even when the roads finally appeared correctly on a map. The last task of the day was finding a chair for Yue's own testimony. The clerk had overlooked the simple fact that a witness might sit when no injury required it. Han's daughter moved a spare stool from the board corner and asked whether its position blocked the passage. It did not. Yue tried the seat, looked at the public sequence and found that her mouth had gone dry.

desert_p22_081.speaker: narrator
desert_p22_081.text: She would speak about things she had seen, which sounded simple until she imagined the room looking back at her. The daughter offered a cup from the room's ordinary town supply. Yue drank and thanked her. Tomorrow she would bring her notes, and enough honesty to leave their gaps visible.
